data.title: Blur Disables Contract Upgrades, Removing an ETH Recovery Route
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, NFT marketplace aggregator Blur has disabled contract upgrades, removing a route for recovering ETH by upgrading contracts. Developer Quit said 545.6 ETH is spread across 315 contracts with no direct withdrawal path. Withdrawals from regular wallets remain available.

data.title: STOCKS | Goldman Traders See US Selloff as Buying Opportunity, Warn of Positioning Risks
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s trading desk says last week’s selloff created an attractive opportunity to buy US stocks. The bank cautions that investor positioning remains elevated, and the broader capitulation it says is needed for a meaningful rally may be missing.

data.title: Eric Trump-Backed Foundation Future Industries Ends Employee Health Benefits Amid Cash Crunch
data.description: According to CNBC, employees at Eric Trump-backed robotics startup Foundation Future Industries were told their health benefits through Rippling had been terminated retroactive to October. A staff memo said workers would be offered COBRA coverage for November, and the company said it would reimburse premiums and was onboarding a new benefits provider. Rippling said Foundation had failed to meet its payroll and benefits obligations for multiple months. Employees were last paid on Oct. 15 and face a third straight pay cycle without income as another scheduled payday approaches on Nov. 30. Foundation has sought a bridge loan while awaiting a possible $150 million investment from South Korean conglomerate Base Group as early as December or January; Base said the investment was under consideration, but funding has not been finalized.

data.title: Solana Foundation Says Alpenglow Upgrade Set for Mid-October to Make Technology Faster, Cheaper and More Resilient
data.description: Solana Foundation Chief Strategy Officer Rachel Conlan said Alpenglow is scheduled for a core upgrade in mid-October that will make the technology faster, cheaper and more resilient. According to Odaily, Solana said in a post on X that representatives from Morgan Stanley, BNY Mellon and DTCC attended Breakpoint; Conlan also said the century-old financial industry is being reimagined.

data.title: Bessent Warns Fed Against Overtightening as US Markets Slide
data.description: US markets swooned as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that the Federal Reserve risks jeopardizing the economy by overtightening in response to the latest inflation data, citing signs of fragility in the financial system, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Jay Clayton Warns of Further Tech Disruptions During System Upgrades
data.description: According to CNBC, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans that technology outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade systems for the AI era. Recent outages disrupted air travel and Microsoft Outlook and slowed bank transactions. Officials have largely dismissed the possibility that the outages were linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack. The Federal Aviation Administration said router upgrades caused a data flood that prompted a nationwide ground stop just over a week ago and that there was no indication of a cyberattack. Microsoft said an earlier network capacity upgrade caused the Outlook outage.

data.title: Delta System Outage Delays Flights to and From Atlanta Across the United States
data.description:
According to Jin10, the Federal Aviation Administration said Sunday that a problem with an aircraft weight-and-balance calculation system delayed all Delta flights to and from Atlanta. The average delay was about one hour. Affected flights included Delta departures from the continental United States to Atlanta and flights departing Atlanta; the delay procedures applied only to Delta.

The system calculates an aircraft’s total weight, including its airframe, fuel, passengers, and baggage, and helps pilots determine the center of gravity and whether the load is balanced. Delta said it was using manual backup procedures to ensure flights could depart safely while its teams worked to restore the automated system. The airline said it was coordinating with air traffic control to ease congestion at its Atlanta hub.

data.title: Greer: Thailand to Cut Tariffs on All Goods Exported to the U.S.
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, U.S. Trade Representative Greer said Thailand will lower tariffs on all goods exported to the United States.

data.title: Bessent: Market Selloff Driven by Fed Remarks, Midterm Elections and Other Factors
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the market selloff stemmed from Federal Reserve remarks, the midterm elections and other factors. He said officials have no answers yet about Nvidia’s chip sales and need further responses, adding that they are in contact with the company’s interim leadership and lawyers. Bessent said there were no untraceable handshake-deal transactions and that officials need to identify Nvidia’s head of compliance and determine which levels of the company knew about the matter. He expressed confidence that the relevant committee would quickly establish the facts.

data.title: Yardeni Trims S&P 500 Year-End Forecast Again, Says Bear Market Is Unlikely
data.description: According to Bloomberg, strategist Ed Yardeni cut his S&P 500 Index year-end forecast for a second time in about two months after a powerful stock selloff pushed the benchmark into a technical correction. He said a bear market is unlikely.

data.title: Chile Central Bank Governor Rosanna Costa Says Recovery Could Take Longer
data.description: Chile’s economic recovery could take longer because there are no clear signs that investment is rebounding, Central Bank Governor Rosanna Costa said in an interview with El Mercurio published on Sunday, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Cysic CEO: Public Keys for More Than 6M BTC Exposed On-Chain
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing CoinDesk, Cysic CEO Leo Fan said Bitcoin’s key response to quantum threats is migrating funds, as upgrading cryptography alone would not be enough. Glassnode data showed that in October, public keys for more than 6 million BTC—31.2% of the circulating supply—were exposed on-chain.

Fan said standards exist for single-signature post-quantum signatures, while threshold-signature and multisignature solutions remain under research. Custodians and cross-chain bridges would also need to modify their systems. BIP 361, which would gradually restrict transactions from wallets that have not upgraded, and BIP 360 remain drafts. Developers are divided over mandatory freezes versus voluntary upgrades.
